turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: At the Sea of Cortez Forum in Los Cabos last week, someone stood up and proposed a treaty signed by five states.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Five states to decide together how investment moves and how the sea stays protected.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Hans Herrmann from Mare Nostrum said the region already has the talent and the ties north, but no shared planning tool.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the idea is one document, community voices included, to steer both growth and conservation.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meanwhile Agustín Coppel opened the same summit calling for the whole region to double its economy and triple foreign investment inside 20 years.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That would mean steady 3.5 percent growth every year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Starting from the 4.1 billion dollars now coming in from abroad.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And yet the same Los Cabos that hosts these talks received only 2.02 million pesos in state water-works money across five years.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050. Today we sit with that gap between the big numbers on stage and the quiet numbers on the ground.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The question we keep coming back to is simple: what does it take for a place to grow without outrunning its own water and light?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Foro Mar de Cortés summit just wrapped in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The light down there always feels different this time of year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It does.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What stood out for you?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Agustín Coppel opened by calling for 3.5 percent annual growth across the five states for the next 20 years.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That would double the whole regional economy.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly, and he wants foreign investment tripled from the current four point one billion dollars.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Almost ten percent of what Mexico receives altogether.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: He urged more public investment in roads, ports, airport use, education and security.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Tus Buenas Noticias covered the event under the motto Taking the Helm.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They also noted the forum ranks Baja California Sur first in natural capital for the region.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That feels like the quiet advantage we rarely name out loud.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Coppel pointed out that Baja California Sur itself grew only two point one percent a year over the last decade.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the gap between where we are and where he wants us to go is quite wide.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The agenda touched limits to development and marine conservation too.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep picturing the swell rolling in while they talk about those limits.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: He asked for more public money in roads, ports, airports, education and security to close it.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would that actually look like on the ground here?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A few days later Hans Herrmann from Mare Nostrum took the stage with another idea.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The regional treaty.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes, a five-state agreement among Baja California, Baja California Sur, Nayarit, Sinaloa and Sonora.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: To guide both investment and conservation together.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: He said the region already has talent, infrastructure and close ties to the United States, yet still lacks the planning tools.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the treaty would be the missing instrument.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Foro Mar de Cortés would convene it with real community participation.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep thinking about how the desert and the sea would shape those planning meetings if communities really led the way.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Hans Herrmann made the point that the missing piece is exactly those shared instruments for deciding together.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you ask the people in the villages if they were at the table?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Whether the new investment would protect the places they have fished for generations or just open them up.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. The long road south always brings those questions back to the water's edge. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep wondering what that participation would feel like in a fishing village south of here.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The summit ran from the tenth to the twelfth of November.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It was the sixth edition, after all.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They brought in IMCO to talk regional competitiveness.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the future of cities too.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Climate change sat on the agenda right beside marine conservation.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert teaches patience, but the sea does not wait. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Or if the desert and the sea simply keep their own pace. [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: La Paz sits as the state capital with its bay and port facing the water.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: People there move between government offices and the university, the lowest municipal poverty at 20.6 percent.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The bay must shape how the city grows, yet aquifers 0324 and 0313 sit in deficit. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes, and that tight water-energy coupling shows up in every new neighborhood.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Drive north and you reach Todos Santos–El Pescadero, the Pacific amenity spine.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Lifestyle migrants arrive for the culture and the light, yet the same aquifers feel the pressure.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does a morning walk along that coast sound like when new homes keep appearing?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The highway and the shoreline both feel the squeeze of growth. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos holds the primate municipality role, 351111 people across 428 localities.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Its hotels line the corridor, from Grand Velas to Vidanta, drawing visitors year-round.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Those properties sit on aquifers already marked in deficit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly, and the East Cape and Cabo Pulmo remain points of tension.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: At the recent Los Cabos summit, Hans Herrmann spoke of a five-state regional treaty.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: He wants investment guided by shared planning for the Sea of Cortez.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Agustín Coppel called for doubling the regional economy over 20 years.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That would mean 3.5 percent annual growth across the five states.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Tripling foreign investment while adding roads, ports, and education.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: BCS itself grew only 2.1 percent a year over the last decade, so the jump feels steep.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would a fisher in Comondú or a family in Loreto ask about that plan? [breath]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Comondú carries the agro pole in Valle Santo Domingo, yet lacks a public cadastre viewer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Loreto keeps its POEL from 2014 while the Nopoló corridor grows quietly.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The desert light and the long road south still decide how daily life unfolds in each place.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep wondering how those towns would answer a simple question about water and time.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Hans Herrmann from Mare Nostrum mentioned talent and US ties already in place.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The treaty would include Baja California, Nayarit, Sinaloa and Sonora too.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Community participation would guide every decision on conservation and new projects.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Agustín Coppel noted current foreign investment sits near 4.1 billion dollars.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. That figure is roughly ten percent of Mexico's total, yet the road ahead still needs building.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I wonder what the swell sounds like on the Pacific side when the next home rises.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The numbers on water works keep pointing back to the same line under the map.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias laid it out last week. Los Cabos received just 2.02 million from the state water agency over five years.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: While La Paz took 121.38 million and Mulegé 126.99. The desert asks the same question every time: where does the next drop come from?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet the real-estate numbers from JLL show Los Cabos still captured 81 percent of the state’s residential volume.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That mismatch is the thread. Growth keeps arriving, but the pipe and the wire do not stretch at the same speed.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: El Mundo Digital spoke with the tourism developers. They listed water first, then roads, then power capacity.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the urban plan itself is back on the table.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal’s earlier Foresight notes already called water the political brake on tourism investment. Nothing new there, only louder now.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The knowledge graph keeps tagging the same signal: SIBCS as an energy island. The grid sits alone.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Reliability and investment both hit the ceiling at the same time. One storm or one pump failure and the lights and the taps feel it together.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the hidden thread is not just the missing money. It is the shared limit between water and power that no single project can outrun.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The 2026 POEL consultation adds one more layer. Developers must now bring their own desalination and treatment.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That shifts the old bargain. The municipality used to promise the lines; now the lines travel with the permit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Some residents already wait 40 days for a connection and pay 2,000 pesos every two weeks for truck deliveries.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert does not negotiate. It simply waits for the next bill to arrive.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The surprise is how little the state line has moved while private money keeps flowing in. [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Maybe the thread runs the other way. Perhaps the ceiling is not the money at all, but the rule that still treats the island grid as an afterthought.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal’s past editions already flagged the same spot. Water, grid, and place set the 2050 limit together.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A road or a pipe is never only concrete. It is the quiet agreement about how far the city is allowed to reach.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: When that agreement stays unwritten, every new hotel and every empty cistern tells the same story.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Did you know 22 of 39 aquifers sit in deficit right now?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That number feels heavy. [pause] What does it look like on the ground?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: CONAGUA measured the whole state pulling 105.1 cubic hectometers more than it receives each year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Imagine the desert trying to refill a single backyard cistern while the tap stays open.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: INEGI counted exactly 798,447 residents living in Baja California Sur according to the 2020 census data.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The economy produced 187,152 million pesos in constant prices through 2024, showing a 3.5 percent rise from the year before.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. [chuckle] The cistern never catches up.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And this is the same place courting big new hotels and airports.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Sea of Cortez Forum heard Agustín Coppel call for 3.5 percent growth every year for 20 years.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. That ambition meets the leaking cistern.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Baja California Sur grew only 2.1 percent a year over the last decade.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the new target asks the desert for more than it has given lately.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Los Cabos POEL now requires every new project to add its own desal plant or wastewater treatment before it can build.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the rule tries to make the bucket watertight.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Los Cabos Hotel Association reported tourism sales down between 25 and 35 percent over the past two years, with at least 27 restaurants now closed.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: At the same time the transport ministry is spending 350 million pesos on conserving roads and bridges throughout the state.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It does. The council just opened consultation on the El Tezal partial plan and the Punta Nayu project.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you ask the planners if you sat at that table?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Whether the desert will still lend us water after the next summers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A fair question. [breath] The light on the water always makes the answer feel possible.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The federal investment in social programs for the state totals 6766000000 MXN this year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That sits alongside plans for a 240 megawatt power plant in Los Cabos expected by 2028.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It does. Yet the numbers keep reminding us the cistern is finite.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: IMCO tracked the state climbing from eighth to fifth in competitiveness lately.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That climb sits right beside the water warnings.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Los Cabos Hotel Association saw visitor numbers drop from the north. [laugh]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep thinking about a single house going up in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The kind you see in the JLL numbers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. One house, yet it sits inside a whole mesh of rules no one sees from the street.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? Like what kind of rules do you picture first?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The 2026 POEL consultation now asks developers to supply their own desalination and treatment.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the house carries its own small water plant before the first wall goes up.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. That requirement comes straight from the mesas on agua and urbanismo Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Which ones meet with SEPUIMM and IMPLAN.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And with the G20 quality-infrastructure principles that ask for long-term output specs.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Wait—does that also tie into the mesa on desarrollo orientado al transporte?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It does. The same working tables look at how transit benefits ripple out, the way the VTPI framework lays them out.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep picturing the road out front, quiet at dawn, carrying more than cars once the house is lived in.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the hidden design is not the roofline. It is the document that says the roof must also handle its own waste stream.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The same mesas track the tourism investment signal against the water limit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One number from last year still sits in the room: one point five seven billion dollars in BCS residential volume.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos took 81 percent of that.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yet the grid that keeps the lights on is still treated as an energy island.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: CFE reliability inside the isolated system sets the real ceiling.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the house also carries its own piece of the larger reliability question.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would you ask the people around those tables if you could sit in for one session?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I would ask how the rules for one house scale when the next follow.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The working tables keep pulling those threads together before the next permit is signed.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A quiet kind of design, [pause] written in the margins of the mesas.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Ha, of course it is. [chuckle] One more detail from the JLL report: 1,840 units sold across the state.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Each one quietly shaped by the same unseen documents.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal’s Visión pillar on housing points straight at the risk.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Housing grows where services are missing or where water and coastlines are already under pressure.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The state counted 798,447 people in the 2020 census. That number sets the scale.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Really? One number like that makes the whole picture feel more immediate.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Housing accounts for just one item this week, with the EWMA at 1.81.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yet no published target exists for how many units should stand by 2050.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The aspiration is simple: homes with real services, set back from the first line of risk.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And matched to whatever water and energy margin actually exists.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The levers are clear. First, move what is already exposed before opening new coastal fronts.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Then cross-check every project against the demand–supply board and current plans.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Treat the backlog of missing services as a hard ceiling, not something the market will fix later.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. That changes how growth is allowed to happen.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: When you drive through Comondú the fields stretch out under that clear sky and you see the room it has.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. It turns the question from how much we can build into whether the place can actually hold it.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you ask the planners in Loreto about keeping that balance with the protected areas?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Tendencia 2050 sees the state as a polycentric system rather than one repeated coastal pattern.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos keeps the tourism engine but carries water and power stress.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: East Cape stays in tension with protected areas.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Todos Santos and El Pescadero form the Pacific amenity spine.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: La Paz serves as the water–energy node and service capital.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Loreto anchors tourism and conservation. Comondú holds the agricultural role with more room.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Northern Mulegé remains thinly documented, now seeing a remote generation tender.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Northern Mulegé with its tender feels like the quiet edge of the map.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Each place keeps its own vocation instead of copying the same formula.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: New growth only where water and energy show real margin or come from desal, without counting on NOM-011 credit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: East Cape and Loreto respect ANP and POEL limits before any scaling.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would it take, really, for those different roles to stay distinct all the way out?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Each vocation contributes a distinct role, not diluted Cabos statewide. [pause] The light on the desert changes everything when you drive north.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Comondú and the north could add production without emptying services or protected zones.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The aspiration stays grounded in those local roles and the real margins of water and energy across the state.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That is the watchlist that matters. [chuckle] The sea keeps its own count.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep wondering what it really means for this place to grow in a way that makes sense for everyone who lives here.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Not just bigger, but right. Something that feels natural rather than forced onto the land.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. Like the buildings and the roads actually belong here instead of sitting on top of everything.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Instead of fighting the desert and the sea for space, as if they weren't already part of the story.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would that look like, do you think? [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Maybe houses that sit back a little from the edge, where the water can still reach the land in its own time.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the light can move through them the way it always has across the dunes and the water.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That feels like the real work ahead of us now. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The forum's vision of protecting the Sea of Cortez while attracting investment comes to mind here. [breath]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. Not how much we add to the map, but whether it still feels like home when we are done with it all.
